description: A restore verification spec defines how database backups are tested and verified — RTO targets, integrity check procedures, automated drill schedules, and checksum methods. An unverified backup is not a backup.

rules.description: The spec must declare rto_hours, drill_schedule, integrity_checks, and checksum_method.
rto_hours must be a concrete positive number. Vague descriptions (fast, acceptable, tbd) cannot be measured against actual restore drill results and are rejected.
integrity_checks must be a non-empty array with at least one row_count or count_compare check. Without row count verification, partial restores and truncated tables go undetected.
drill_schedule must declare a frequency (monthly minimum for production, weekly for RPO < 4h) and automated: true. Manual drills are unreliable and often skipped.

checksum_method must be a recognized machine-verifiable method: pg_dump_sha256, pg_dump_md5, table_count, table_checksum, pitr_lsn, or custom (with description). Vague values like manual or visual are rejected.
